rv.q: The piece is an excellent business card: her observations are acute and well-calibrated, her performance is witty and thoroughly engaging.
Minor gripes aside Ms HSB has the chutzpah to deliver a yarn with confidence albeit the material would benefit from a slower and clear narrative arc.
A towering performance from an extremely talented writer and performer.
As it is, this is a great show: bold, funny and compelling.
In Florence, writer and performer Honor Santa Barnes explores the uncomfortable truth that talent and hard work sometimes aren't enough to open doors.
It is funny, disarming, and occasionally disturbing, and is certainly helped by Honor's personable performance...

cn.t: Honor Santa Barnes's solo show earns mostly strong notices for its sharp script and disciplined performance. Critics are divided on depth, but its art-world identity satire lands as a compelling, if uneven, character study.
